# Server configuration that produced these fixtures.
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
  --max-model-len 2048 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --port 8000

# Environment required on this box (RTX 3060 Ti, 8GB, driver 595.71.05):
CUDA_HOME=<venv>/lib/python3.14/site-packages/nvidia/cu13
PATH=<venv>/bin:$CUDA_HOME/bin:$PATH
VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0

# Why VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0: flashinfer 0.6.14 bundles CCCL headers
# that fail to compile against the CUDA 13.3 toolkit shipped in the cu13
# wheels ("CUDA compiler and CUDA toolkit headers are incompatible").
# Only the sampling kernels are affected; attention and CUDA graph capture
# work. Falls back to the native PyTorch sampler. Does not change which
# metrics /metrics emits, but IS a deviation from a stock install and should
# be revisited on the H100.
#
# gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 (not 0.85): desktop/Chromium hold ~865 MiB, so
# 0.85 requested 6.5 GiB against 6.29 GiB free and failed at startup.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The `saturated` condition used a SECOND server config, identical except:
#   --max-num-seqs 4        (driven with 32 concurrent clients)
#
# Why: with the default batch size, 391,952 tokens of KV cache gave 191x max
# concurrency, so 16 concurrent requests never queued and
# num_requests_waiting stayed 0 across idle/single/burst. A fixture set where
# the queue-depth signal never leaves zero cannot validate the parser field
# that matters most. Capping the running batch at 4 forces the excess into
# the waiting queue: running=4, waiting=28, reason="capacity"=28.
#
# KNOWN GAPS (measured, not assumed):
#
# vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc IS exercised but only at the very low end. Observed
# maxima: idle 0.0, single 0.000408, burst 0.00498, saturated 0.00151 -- i.e.
# the cache never exceeds ~0.5% utilisation. Short prompts against 391,952
# tokens of cache. The metric parses and moves; what is unvalidated is its
# behaviour under memory pressure, which is the regime that actually changes
# decode behaviour. (An earlier version of this file said "reads 0.00 in all
# four conditions" -- that was a formatting artifact of printing at two
# decimal places, and was wrong.)
#
# vllm:num_preemptions_total and vllm:estimated_flops_per_gpu_total are flat
# zero in all four conditions. These are genuinely unexercised: present in the
# scrape, parseable, but no fixture has ever seen them non-zero.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# H100 CAPTURE CHECKLIST (do not rediscover this on rented time)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Re-run the four conditions above; metric names may have moved if the vLLM
#    version differs. Fixtures are per-version by directory for this reason.
# 2. Close the kv_cache_usage_perc gap: long prompts / large model, driven
#    until the cache is the binding constraint rather than max-num-seqs.
#    That is the fixture that validates the high end of the range.
# 3. Try to exercise vllm:num_preemptions_total -- oversubscribe until vLLM
#    preempts. Preemption is a pressure signal the controller will want.
# 4. Check whether vllm:estimated_flops_per_gpu_total populates on datacenter
#    hardware; it is flat zero here and may be architecture-gated.
# 5. Re-run verify_energy_agreement under varying load on that GPU. Sensor
#    cadence and ring depth are per-device; so is counter trustworthiness.
# 6. Re-check whether VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 is still needed.
# 7. MULTI-GPU: if the node has more than one card, live-verify gpu_guard's
#    device-identity gate. It has only ever run against the fake NVML layer.
#      a. `gpu_guard --gpu 1 lock --mhz <x> --crash-after 3 ...` to strand a
#         record for GPU 1.
#      b. `gpu_guard --gpu 0 status`  -> must report OTHER DEVICE and
#         recommend `--gpu 1`, NOT recommend a bare restore.
#      c. `gpu_guard --gpu 0 restore` -> must refuse with a device-identity
#         mismatch, leave GPU 0's power limit untouched, and leave GPU 1's
#         record restored=false. Exit code 1.
#      d. `gpu_guard --gpu 1 restore` -> must succeed and clear the record.
#    If (c) mis-caps GPU 0 or clears the record, STOP: recovery is applying one
#    card's snapshot to another and the sweep cannot be trusted on that node.
